flashcards.front: What is the primary threat vector for Suspicious Website Logins?
flashcards.back_definition: Adversaries exploit low-entropy passwords on authentication endpoints to bypass standard perimeter security controls.
flashcards.back_example: Example: Status: Failed logon | Attempts: 40 in 10 seconds from IP 198.51.100.99
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse this threat with other layers (like physical breaches or certificate revocations) which target different assets.
flashcards.back_hook: Recall: low-entropy passwords is the unlocked door; authentication endpoints is what the attacker wants to steal.

flashcards.front: How does the security team mitigate Suspicious Website Logins threats?
flashcards.back_definition: Deploying and enforcing Multi-Factor Authentication and API rate limiters directly hardens authentication endpoints and blocks unauthorized connections.
flashcards.back_example: Action: Update security configurations to require Multi-Factor Authentication and API rate limiters.
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse mitigation (actively blocking the exploit) with detection (simply logging or alerting the event).
flashcards.back_hook: Mitigation is the shield; detection is the security camera.

flashcards.front: How do analysts detect exploitation of Suspicious Website Logins?
flashcards.back_definition: By auditing event data and implementing logic flags built to alert on failed authentication rate threshold audits.
flashcards.back_example: Syslog trace: Status: Failed logon | Attempts: 40 in 10 seconds from IP 198.51.100.99
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse signature-based detection (matching known strings) with anomaly-based detection (mapping dynamic standard deviations).
flashcards.back_hook: Detection is looking for the fingerprint left behind by the threat.
